name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
principle: Code builds a data-store query by embedding unneutralized data into query syntax. Special query characters can change selection logic, append commands, or alter returned records.
detection_signals: user-controlled value concatenated into LDAP filter passed to DirContext.search
user-controlled value concatenated into XPathExpression via XPath.compile
user-controlled value concatenated into XQuery/DQL/HTSQL query string before execution
MongoDB/NoSQL query built from raw JSON string concatenation or Document.parse(userInput)
query text contains operators like OR, AND, $, //, *, ; adjacent to variables or request parameters
PreparedStatement/parameter API unavailable while query contains '+' or StringBuilder.append(userInput)
negative_signals: JDBC PreparedStatement with ? placeholders and setString/setInt/setObject for all external values
JPA/SQL named parameters with setParameter for all external values
LDAP filter values escaped with LdapName/Rdn.escapeValue or equivalent RFC 4515 escaping before DirContext.search
XPath variables resolved through XPathVariableResolver instead of string concatenation
MongoDB query built with typed Filters.eq/and/or APIs, not JSON string concatenation
allowlisted field/order names mapped to constants before inclusion in query syntax
false_defense_traps: escaping only single quotes while other query metacharacters remain active
blacklisting strings like OR, AND, SELECT, or $ instead of using parameters
client-side validation before server-side query construction
wrapping input in quotes without escaping or binding
using stored procedures that concatenate untrusted input into dynamic query strings
verification_focus: Can any untrusted value reach query syntax as text instead of a parameter, escaped literal, or allowlisted identifier?

consequence_chains.trigger: untrusted data is concatenated into an SQL command
consequence_chains.consequence: read, modify, or delete database data; bypass access control

consequence_chains.trigger: untrusted data is concatenated into an LDAP filter
consequence_chains.consequence: alter directory search results or bypass authentication checks

consequence_chains.trigger: untrusted data is concatenated into an XPath expression
consequence_chains.consequence: select unintended XML nodes or bypass credential checks

consequence_chains.trigger: untrusted data is concatenated into an XQuery expression
consequence_chains.consequence: read or manipulate unintended XML data

patch_principle: Use parameterized query APIs for every data value.
Escape query-language literals with the correct library when parameters are unavailable.
Allowlist and map identifiers such as column names, sort fields, and collection names.
Do not concatenate request, file, environment, or database-derived data into query text.
Keep authorization checks independent of attacker-controllable query result ordering or count.

minimal_examples.vuln: ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM items WHERE owner='" + user + "' AND itemname='" + item + "'");
minimal_examples.safe: PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM items WHERE owner=? AND itemname=?"); ps.setString(1, user); ps.setString(2, item);
